name: Question 15
problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,j$ meters. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.
worked_solution:
**Method 1**

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(r(t))^{′} \\  & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector. 

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =(v(t))^{′} \\  & =(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-16\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i-16\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the magnitude of the acceleration as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}||a(t)|| & =\sqrt{(-16\operatorname{cos}⁡4t)^{2}+(-16\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{16}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡4t+{16}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡4t} \\  & =\sqrt{{16}^{2}} \\  & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the magnitude of the acceleration is $16\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

Note that $||a||$ is constant, but $a$ is not. 

**Method 2**

For uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane, we have

$$
a=-{\omega }^{2}r\,⇒\,||a||={\omega }^{2}||r||.
$$

In our case, the radius of the circle is $a=1\,\text{m}$ and the angular frequency $\omega =4\,\text{rad/s}.$ Therefore,

$$
||a||={4}^{2}\cdot 1=16\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.
$$

html:
Question 15
?

An object moves along a circular path with position r(t)=cos⁡4ti+sin⁡4tj meters. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of the object at time t, measured in seconds.

a
4m/s2
b
2m/s2
c
16m/s2
d
64m/s2
e
8m/s2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get v(t)=(r(t))′=(cos⁡4ti+sin⁡4tj)′=−4sin⁡4ti+4cos⁡4tj

Then, we find the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector. a(t)=(v(t))′=(−4sin⁡4ti+4cos⁡4tj)′=−16cos⁡4ti−16sin⁡4tj.

Finally, we calculate the magnitude of the acceleration as follows: ||a(t)||=(−16cos⁡4t)2+(−16sin⁡4t)2=162cos2⁡4t+162sin2⁡4t=162=16

Therefore, the magnitude of the acceleration is 16m/s2.

Note that ||a|| is constant, but a is not.

Method 2

For uniform circular motion in the xy-plane, we have

a=−ω2r⇒||a||=ω2||r||.

In our case, the radius of the circle is a=1m and the angular frequency ω=4rad/s. Therefore,

||a||=42⋅1=16m/s2.
